wi_7_3_horse_rampart.blurb: Horse Rampart is a wall of roughly 200 feet in length perched on the east side of Devil's Lake, above a talus slope and boulder field in the Baraboo Range. The routes are fairly long and mostly moderate, which makes it a good stop for climbers building up on traditional gear. Expect trad leads and top-rope laps from beginner-level climbs up through the low 5.10s, with a small handful of hard test pieces in the 5.11 to 5.12 range. The ground at the base is comfortable for gearing up. The wall sits a little higher on the bluff than its neighbors near the railroad tracks.

wi_1_smooth_operator_area.blurb: A bouldering zone at the far northern end of Devil's Lake's West Bluff, with the problems scattered through talus just under a band of cliff. Walks from the trail are short, from under a minute to several minutes, so it is an easy place to drop in for a quick session. The grade spread is wide: a good handful of easy problems from VB to V2, a solid middle of V3 to V5, and a hard tail reaching into double-digit V grades, including a few unfinished projects. Some lines are tall with slick tops, so bring several pads and a spotter. Landings sit at the edge of more talus.

wi_12_rainy_wednesday_tower.blurb: A tower on Devil's Lake's East Rampart, with Bill's Buttress on one side and the Leaning Tower Gully on the other. The routes here run long on good rock and are mostly traditional leads, with a few set up only as top-ropes. Grades start at an easy 5.4, bulk up in the 5.7 to 5.8 range, and top out in the low 5.12s, so it suits both newer leaders and strong climbers. The easier lines are sustained and entertaining, with roofs and corners rather than short boulder-style cruxes. It is popular, so getting there early helps you claim a line.

wi_cleo_amphitheater_the.blurb: A bowl-shaped cluster of cliffs on Devil's Lake's West Bluff, among the busiest climbing spots on that side. Its signature feature is a freestanding tower of about 50 feet with a loose-feeling summit block. Climbing is traditional on hard, glassy Baraboo quartzite, with some top-rope-only lines. Grades run from about 5.3 up past 5.10, with a lot of moderates, so it works well for newer leaders who can place their own gear. Ratings can feel stiff on this rock. Weekends bring crowds.

wi_15_pseudo_hawk_s_nest.blurb: A multi-tiered formation along the East Rampart at Devil's Lake, just west of the Leaning Tower Gully. Most of the routes are traditional or top-rope, and the cliff steps up through several levels. The grade range is broad: a gentle 5.4 or so to the 5.13 level, with many climbs in the 5.7 to 5.9 band and a real cluster of hard 5.11 and 5.12 lines. Because it lies west of the gully, it may be quieter than the busier walls to the east. Wind can be noticeable on top.

wi_dudley_davis_quarry_park.blurb: A small abandoned quarry turned neighborhood park on Madison's near west side. It is mostly a bouldering spot, with a few top-rope and trad lines mixed in. Most of the boulder problems are short and fall between VB and V3, with a few V4 and harder lines, and the roped climbs go from about 5.4 to the low 5.11s. The lower terrace gets plenty of sun while the upper terrace stays shaded, so you can pick your side by season. Climbers rarely visit; you will mostly share the place with strollers and local kids.

wi_poison_ivy_wall.blurb: Known as the wall of moderates, this East Bluff wall at Devil's Lake has roughly ten routes between 5.6 and 5.8, which is its main draw. The climbs are short, around 30 to 40 feet, and mostly traditional with top-rope options, plus a handful of boulder problems and a few harder lines up into the 5.10s and low 5.11s. It sits in the West Terrace group of rocks, on the level between Bird-Foot Buttress and White Wall. Cracks and corners dominate, so it is a handy place to practice placing gear on easier terrain.
